title: How evolution fine tunes molecular mechanisms to create and maintain membrane diversity between species

content_html:
The cell membrane is a fundamental biological structure. These lipid layers surround and organize every cell, controlling everything from signaling to transport. But for membranes to function properly, their physicochemical properties must sit within a narrow range: for instance, not too rigid or too fluid.

Since environmental conditions such as variation in dietary lipids or fluctuating temperature may alter membrane fluidity, organisms must regulate themselves. Different organisms have evolved different preferences for the properties of their cellular membranes.

For Snezhka Oliferenko, who leads the Crick's Comparative Biology of Mitotic Division Lab, biological membranes are the perfect system for studying the evolution of cellular diversity across species. "By focusing on how cells build and regulate their membranes, we can uncover how diversity arises," she explains.

"We want to understand how changes in lipid biochemistry affect cell makeup, cell behavior and ultimately, cell evolution."

In their latest study, published in Genes & Development, Oliferenko and her team examined two closely related fission yeast species, Schizosaccharomyces pombe and Schizosaccharomyces japonicus, which share a very similar genetic makeup but are biologically very different.

A key factor in membrane fluidity is the level of "unsaturation," which depends on the type of lipids present. Membranes with a higher proportion of unsaturated lipids that have cis-double bonds in their fatty acid tails are more fluid because kinks in the tails prevent tight packing of lipids. S. pombe produces more flexible, fluid membranes, whereas S. japonicus membranes are more ordered and rigid. These differences provide a natural comparison for understanding how cells can evolve and maintain distinct physicochemical properties of their membranes.

Lead author Elisa Gomez-Gil studied both species in detail, analyzing the lipid composition of the membranes under different conditions and the activity of the genes that control lipid production. "We focused on a key feedback loop involving a protein called Mga2, which sits in the membrane and acts as a sensor," Gomez-Gil describes. "When membranes become too rigid, Mga2 is activated. It is cleaved from the membrane and switches on a gene that produces Ole1, an enzyme that makes unsaturated fatty acids, restoring balance."

Gomez-Gil compared how this system behaves in each yeast species, then went a step further by editing parts of this feedback loop to test how each component behaved in a different biological context. "This allowed us to isolate which elements set the sensitivity of the system and understand how those elements have been tuned through evolution," she adds.

They showed that each species has a different threshold for when the membrane needs adjusting, with S. pombe having a low tolerance for membrane rigidity, and that this was due to two key evolutionary shifts. Small differences in the part of the Mga2 protein that sits next to the membrane alter how readily it is cleaved when the membrane becomes too rigid. At the same time, changes in the Ole1 gene set the baseline level of the response, determining how much of the enzyme is produced once the system is activated.

This shows that the sensor and its downstream response have evolved together, ensuring the system still works even as the underlying membrane biochemistry shifts.

"We often think of evolution as creating new biological machinery," adds Oliferenko. "But in many cases, it's fine-tuning what's already there. Much of the diversity we see across species may not come from entirely new genes or pathways, but from subtle shifts in how shared systems are regulated."

content_html_zh:
细胞膜是基本的生物结构。 这些脂质层包围并组织每个细胞，控制从信号传导到运输的一切。 但为了使膜正常发挥作用，它们的物理化学特性必须在一个狭窄的范围内：例如，不能太刚性或太流动。

由于饮食脂质变化或温度波动等环境条件可能会改变膜的流动性，因此生物体必须进行自我调节。 不同的生物体对其细胞膜的特性产生了不同的偏好。

对于克里克有丝分裂部门比较生物学实验室负责人 Snezhka Oliferenko 来说，生物膜是研究跨物种细胞多样性进化的完美系统。 “通过关注细胞如何构建和调节细胞膜，我们可以揭示多样性是如何产生的，”她解释道。

“我们想了解脂质生物化学的变化如何影响细胞构成、细胞行为以及最终的细胞进化。”

在发表在《Genes & Development》杂志上的最新研究中，Oliferenko 和她的团队检查了两种密切相关的裂殖酵母物种：粟酒裂殖酵母和日本裂殖酵母，它们的基因组成非常相似，但生物学上却截然不同。

膜流动性的一个关键因素是“不饱和度”水平，这取决于存在的脂质类型。 具有较高比例的不饱和脂质且其脂肪酸尾部具有顺式双键的膜的流动性更强，因为尾部的扭结阻止了脂质的紧密堆积。 S。 粟酒裂殖酵母产生更灵活的流体膜，而 S. 日本刺参的膜更加有序和坚硬。 这些差异为了解细胞如何进化和维持其膜的独特理化特性提供了自然的比较。

主要作者 Elisa Gomez-Gil 详细研究了这两个物种，分析了不同条件下膜的脂质组成以及控制脂质产生的基因的活性。 “我们专注于一个关键的反馈环路，涉及一种名为 Mga2 的蛋白质，它位于膜中并充当传感器，”戈麦斯-吉尔描述道。 “当膜变得太硬时，Mga2 就会被激活。 它从膜上裂解下来，并启动产生 Ole1 的基因，Ole1 是一种产生不饱和脂肪酸的酶，从而恢复平衡。”

戈麦斯-吉尔比较了该系统在每种酵母物种中的表现，然后进一步编辑该反馈循环的部分内容，以测试每个组件在不同生物环境中的表现。 “这使我们能够隔离哪些元素设置系统的敏感性，并了解这些元素是如何通过进化进行调整的，”她补充道。

他们表明，每个物种在膜需要调整时都有不同的阈值，其中 S. 粟酒对膜刚性的耐受性较低，这是由于两个关键的进化转变。 当膜变得太硬时，位于膜旁边的 Mga2 蛋白部分的微小差异会改变它被切割的容易程度。 与此同时，Ole1 基因的变化设定了反应的基线水平，决定了系统激活后会产生多少酶。

这表明传感器及其下游响应已经共同进化，确保即使底层膜生物化学发生变化，系统仍然可以工作。

“我们经常认为进化是创造新的生物机器，”奥利弗连科补充道。 “但在很多情况下，它是对已有的内容进行微调。 我们在物种间看到的大部分多样性可能并非来自全新的基因或途径，而是来自共享系统监管方式的微妙变化。”
